A1.justification: Both complete 19-page PDFs describe the same STP convergence study. The main text, algorithm, table, figures and Appendix A can be reliably matched despite formatting changes and shifted appendix pagination.

before.justification: Section 6 reports original simulations comparing STP, RGF and GLD on a 500-dimensional quadratic, with 50 trajectories per algorithm. Figures 1–3 show their convergence behavior.

after.justification: Section 6 retains the original numerical study, reporting 50 trajectories per algorithm and convergence results in Figures 1–3.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 and the analyzed STP step-size schedules are unchanged. The experimental STP implementation also retains uniform-sphere directions and the step size 4/t^0.51.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same 500-dimensional quadratic optimization problem. No dataset, application domain or distinct test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Figures 1–3 retain RGF and GLD as the comparison methods. The RGF sampling revision changes a reported experimental setting, while the comparator membership and update equations remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 6 changes RGF directions from uniformly distributed on the unit sphere in v4 to Gaussian in v5, while retaining mu_t = 10^-4 and h_t = 1/L. This revises a stated experimental setting; the PDFs do not establish that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The trajectory-wise convergence checks and scaled best-iterate analysis in Figures 1–3 remain unchanged. No ablation, sensitivity test, robustness test or additional diagnostic analysis is introduced.

E5.justification: Both versions report 50 trajectories per algorithm and retain the same trajectory plots. Neither introduces seed information, confidence intervals, significance tests or another uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: Figures 1–3 contain identical plot images. The reported findings also remain unchanged: STP and RGF perform competitively, STP is slightly better, and both outperform GLD. No updated result accompanies the revised RGF sampling description.

T1.justification: Assumptions 1–7, Theorems 1–7, supporting lemmas and the Appendix A proofs are unchanged. The experimental objective's theta_n-to-theta_d edit corrects indexing without changing the theoretical analysis.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the same novelty and convergence claims for smooth, convex and strongly convex functions, including almost-sure best-iterate and final-iterate convergence and expectation bounds.

C2.justification: The explanation linking similar STP/RGF performance to similar theoretical complexity remains unchanged. Discussions of assumptions, applicability and limitations of earlier convergence guarantees are also retained.

D1.justification: Section 6 revises RGF's sampler documentation from uniform-sphere sampling to Gaussian sampling, without specifying Gaussian mean or covariance. Numerical hyperparameters remain unchanged, and no code, data-access or hardware information is added.

R1.justification: The bibliography removes ten distinct works not cited in the body or appendix, including Li and Orabona (2019), Khaled and Richtarik (2020), and Kolda et al. (2003). The substantive related-work discussion remains unchanged; Section 6 also removes attribution of the RGF step size to the cited authors.

P1.justification: v5 briefly rewrites the RGF paragraph, corrects the objective's endpoint index from n to d, changes citation style and alphabetizes/reformats references. Section order and almost all explanatory prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: v5 adds ICLR 2025 publication headers, shades Table 1's header and adjusts spacing. Bibliography changes move the appendix's start from page 13 to page 12. The algorithm, table contents and three plots are retained.

improvement.justification: The index correction and bibliography cleanup provide small clarity gains. However, v5 changes RGF's reported sampling distribution while retaining identical plots, without explaining whether this corrects the description of existing runs or reflects a changed experiment; Gaussian parameters are also unspecified. With the central theory and proofs unchanged, this unresolved relationship between protocol and results prevents a reliable net quality judgment.
